programme.title: The Age of Uncertainty
programme.desc: A distinguished international gathering at JK Galbraith's Vermont farm offer their views on the themes outlined in the series and on other major anxieties facing the modern world.

programme.title: The Lost Libraries of Timbuktu
programme.desc: Aminatta Forna tells the story of legendary Timbuktu and its long hidden legacy of hundreds of thousands of ancient manuscripts. With its university founded around the same time as Oxford, Timbuktu is proof that the reading and writing of books have long been as important to Africans as to Europeans.

programme.title: Life of a Mountain: A Year on Scafell Pike
programme.desc: Documentary following a year in the life of England's highest mountain, Scafell Pike, through the eyes of the farmers who work the valleys and fells, those who climb the mountain for pleasure and those who try to protect its slopes.

programme.title: Winter Walks
programme.desc: A coastal walk is the setting for the Poet Laureate's ramble along Yorkshire's enchanting and historic frontier with the North Sea. Starting in Ravenscar, Simon Armitage takes the old `Cinder Track', a disused railway line. Carrying a 360-degree camera, he passes former quarries and brickworks, before taking a beach walk from Boggle Hole to the picture-perfect Robin Hood's Bay. Simon witnesses at first-hand the impact of coastal erosion, and meets farmers and locals.

programme.title: Christmas University Challenge
programme.sub-title: Durham University v University of York
programme.desc: Alumni of Durham University face graduates of the University of York in the third match. Documentary maker Chris Terrill takes the captain's chair for Durham, while YouTuber Tom Scott heads the York team. Jeremy Paxman asks the questions.

programme.title: The Magical World of Moss
programme.desc: Mosses have colonised almost every corner of the earth's surface. Evolving from oceanic algae that emerged onto the land 450 million years ago, these very first terrestrial plants became one of the main sources of oxygen for our evolving planet, helping to transform it from an arid rock into a lush world.

programme.title: Dame Maggie Smith - A Celebration
programme.desc: A special tribute to the celebrated and enigmatic actress Dame Maggie Smith, who remains a mystery to her friends and perhaps also to herself - hear the story of her remarkable life told by those who knew her best as they celebrate her much-loved appearances across film and TV spanning almost 70 years. Maggie, who passed away in September 2024, is beloved the world over for her countless iconic screen performances - in recent years she gained a new level of popularity playing the razor-tongued Lady Violet Crawley in Downton Abbey, but Maggie remained a very private person who had little time for the trappings that came with fame in spite of her success. Using Maggie's own voice as its heartbeat - and featuring personal accounts from close friends and colleagues from across her career - the film tells the story of a girl born in pre-war Essex who took Broadway and the West End by storm against the odds before eventually becoming one of the nation's most popular and respected performers.
